evidence_i_missed: The Fall 2025 Carbon Budget Update (FCS03160) and Spring 2026 Budget Highlights, which contain the much more recent 2024 community GHG inventory (15.2 Mt CO2e) and supersede my reliance on the older 2023 estimates.
The City's explicit forecasting that the entire 176 Mt community carbon budget for 2050 will be completely depleted by 2036.
errors_in_other_reviews: Both Claude and GPT committed the 'intention-vs-outcome' error explicitly warned against in the instructions. They included the City's budgeted estimate of reducing emissions by 180,000 tonnes CO2e over four years via funded projects as 'supporting evidence'. Funding a project or estimating its future impact is a policy promise, not an observed outcome or proof of trajectory compliance.

claims.proposition_evaluated: Edmonton is on track to meet its adopted community greenhouse-gas emissions targets.
claims.interpretation_notes: Interpreted 'on track' as whether the most recent community emissions data aligns with the targets and carbon budget trajectory set out by the City of Edmonton. In Round 2, I incorporated the 2024 inventory data sourced by other reviewers, which replaces the 2023 data I initially relied on, especially since my original primary URL failed verification.

supporting_evidence.finding: Per-capita community emissions have fallen 46% from the 2005 baseline (to 12.8 tonnes CO2e in 2024), and absolute community emissions are 9% below 2005.
supporting_evidence.source_title: Fall 2025 Carbon Budget Update, 2023-2026 Carbon Budget (FCS03160), pp. 2, 4
supporting_evidence.source_publisher: City of Edmonton, Financial and Corporate Services
supporting_evidence.establishes: Some measured progress in emissions reduction relative to 2005, though insufficient to meet the absolute target trajectories.

challenging_evidence.finding: The City's Fall 2025 Carbon Budget Update reports 2024 community emissions of 15.2 million tCO2e against a required trajectory of 12.2 million tCO2e, directly stating the 2025 target will not be met.
challenging_evidence.source_title: Fall 2025 Carbon Budget Update, 2023-2026 Carbon Budget (FCS03160), pp. 2-3
challenging_evidence.source_publisher: City of Edmonton, Financial and Corporate Services
challenging_evidence.establishes: The City's own official assessment that community emissions exceed targets by roughly 3.0 Mt CO2e and that milestones are out of reach.
challenging_evidence.quote: The trend for this year indicates this target will not be met and there are no current initiatives or actions that will allow the necessary reductions to meet the target.

challenging_evidence.finding: The 176 million tonnes CO2e community carbon budget, designed to last until 2050, is forecast to be fully depleted by 2036.
challenging_evidence.source_title: Fall 2025 Carbon Budget Update, 2023-2026 Carbon Budget (FCS03160), pp. 2, 4, 7
challenging_evidence.source_publisher: City of Edmonton, Financial and Corporate Services
challenging_evidence.establishes: The long-term 2050 target trajectory is completely off track, with the cumulative emissions allowance expected to be exhausted 14 years early.
challenging_evidence.quote: The Carbon Budget continues to deplete at a rate consistent with prior projections, which is expected to hinder the City's ability to achieve established reduction targets.

challenging_evidence.finding: The prior-year miss was also on the record: 2023 community emissions were an estimated 16.2 million tonnes CO2e against a 13.4 million tonne aim, reported by CBC from the Fall 2024 update.
challenging_evidence.source_title: Edmonton fails to meet climate targets 2 years after launching carbon budget (CBC News, Natasha Riebe)
challenging_evidence.establishes: The off-track finding is a multi-year pattern (both 2023 and 2024 trajectories were missed), rather than an isolated anomaly.

limitations: The inventory figures are the City's own self-reported measurements and include modeled estimates for certain sectors.
The 2005 baseline was recalculated due to revised natural gas data, meaning comparisons of percentage drops with older reports require caution.
The 2025 full community GHG inventory data (for the first major milestone year) was not yet published at the time of these reports.
unknowns: Whether the Council's updated Climate Action Plan (2027-2030) resulted in revised, potentially lower numerical targets after early 2026.
The exact magnitude of the 2025 target miss, pending final publication of the 2025 GHG inventory.

missing_evidence.description: Finalized 2025 community GHG inventory confirming the exact size of the missed 2025 milestone.

calculations_needed: Subtracting the required 2024 trajectory (12.2 Mt) from actual 2024 emissions (15.2 Mt) as reported by the City shows a gap of 3.0 Mt CO2e above the trajectory.
what_would_change_my_verdict: A newer official City inventory showing actual emissions falling below the trajectory required by the adopted targets.
Official City Council adoption of drastically relaxed targets such that current emissions levels are re-classified as 'on track'.
claims.suggested_one_line: Edmonton is failing to meet its community greenhouse gas reduction targets, with the City's late 2025 carbon budget update confirming 2024 emissions were 3 million tonnes above the required trajectory.
claims.suggested_short_answer: No. According to the City of Edmonton's Fall 2025 Carbon Budget Update, community emissions in 2024 were 15.2 million tonnes CO2e, missing the target trajectory of 12.2 million tonnes. The City explicitly stated that the 2025 target will not be met with current initiatives, and forecasts that the entire carbon budget meant to last until 2050 will be exhausted by 2036.
suggested_tldr: Edmonton set a community carbon budget to track progress toward becoming carbon-neutral by 2050, with interim milestones in 2025 and 2030.
A Fall 2025 update from the City revealed 2024 emissions were 15.2 million tonnes, exceeding the required trajectory by 3 million tonnes.
The City acknowledges that current actions are insufficient to meet the 2025 target and projects the entire 2050 carbon budget will be depleted 14 years early.
While per-capita emissions have dropped 46% since 2005, absolute emissions reductions are far behind the required pace.
